original.description: The User Management Service contract will encompass a comprehensive suite of offeringsdesigned to support and enhance user interactions and experience for ESA and Third PartyEO Missions.This service contract aims at integrating the User Communication and Information Portaltogether with the User Management functions, covered in the past by separate contracts,whereby ensuring autonomy to Industry in designing and using communication tools asadditional instrument to reach and stimulate a dynamic and variegated user community.The Information Portal is expected to provide seamless access to relevant content and data,Graphical and Editorial Servicesshall deliver visually engaging and professionally curatedmaterials, and finally User Experience Benchmarking Services enable performancecomparisons and insights. A dedicated User Help Desk completes the suite assisting userswith inquiries and technical support, ensuring prompt and effective resolution of issues.User Management Services will implement personalized access to tools, resources, andaccount features through the management of authorisation and authentication services withprovision of a secured User Area. The User Management service will foster a user-centricapproach that prioritizes accessibility, support, and continuous improvement driven by userfeedback.The User Management Service contract shall include the following services: Operations, maintenance and evolutions of the web services for data discoveryaccess and retrieval of Earth Observation products and information (composed byEarth Online, eoPortal, Swarm Data Handbook, EarthCARE Data Handbook, 3DVisuals and Quality Reports Advanced Search platforms). Content Management and Creation, including editorial and graphical services. Operations, maintenance and evolutions of an identity access management infrastructure with federated identity access configurations. Support to user community via a unique and integrated user help desk which serves as the single point of contact for answering to user enquiries and complaints, facilitating data access requests, monitoring and ensuring user satisfaction, and providing communications about system unavailability. The user help desk function will also provide AI powered chatbots and virtual support assistants being powered by a comprehensive and well-maintained and updated knowledgebase. Management of data access requests, assign authorisation to users for accessing restrained data, in agreement to applicable terms and condition (including quota management). Management of a large set of user profiles, including asecure and personalised self managementarea to access and manage account information, access settings and transaction history tracking support requests. By centralizing these functions, the userarea enhances convenience, engagement, and control, allowing users to efficiently interact with the system and AI powered virtual assistant while ensuring their dataand preferences are protected.  User experience benchmarking services for systematic analysing and monitoring of user and stakeholder feedback (surveys and behaviour analytics) and monitor performance to help identifying strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement

original.description: Multiple studies on "Industrialisation of mid-size platforms for LEO constellations in Earth Observation".  This activity is part of the "vertical axis" of the M-IND (Mid-size satellite INDustrialisation) initiative and it is intended for mid-size satellite integrators in order to support the scaling-up of the production of European mid-size satellite (100-500 kg) for Earth Observation applications with LEO constellations. It complements the "horizontal axis" of M-IND, where separate technology activities, mostly fundedunder GSTP, will support Equipment suppliers to modernise and industrialise Equipment for sub-systems in mid-size satellites.This activity will focus on the definition and establishment of credible industrialisation roadmaps covering production ramp-up of full mid-size satellites for Earth Observation, including supply chain strategies covering interchangeability and interoperability of sub-system from multiple suppliers, modular platform architectures including modernisation of capabilities like for example low latency communication via Intersatellite Links (ISL), suitability for several types of Earth Observation payloads, and sustainability aspectsfor zero debris mitigation at end of mission life and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The envisaged solutions and roadmaps shall enable cost-efficient, resilient and high-rate manufacturing aligned with future institutional and commercial mission needs in the EarthObservation domain.

original.description: ObjectivesTo increase the efficiency of photobioreactors by an improved design of light conduction anddiffusion inside the reactor.DescriptionThe need for regenerative life support systems for long term space missions necessitates a questfor increased efficiency of Photobioreactors. The light intensification of photobioreactors is animportant building block to increase the return on investment with respect to light energy introducedvs oxygen yield in a defined volume.Previous activities have identified as a priority the need to progress on specific technologies, suchas the type of light sources and on innovative materials for light conductionand diffusion (e.g.polymers, leaking rods, specific optical fibers, lightning fabrics). This activity attempts to push theboundaries of photobioractor efficiency even further (compared to BIORAT-1) by investigating amore efficient light diffusion and as well characterization of the impact on the process and thebiomass.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review the state of the art for light intensified photobioreactiors and energy efficient lightguidance systems- Design a test bench with realistic operational parameters (light, flow, active species etc.)and test the most optimal configuration to achieve best possible efficiency w.r.t. volumetricoxygen and biomass production- Assess the potential biological effects of immersed light sources and possiblecountermeasures against fouling and clogging- Provide a development plan for operational hardware on ground and in space includingMAIT aspects for an operational scenario and define the scaling laws.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. original.description: EL1-134 - This activity will investigate innovative techniques to enable continuous optical timing and ranging links under all weather conditions, addressing a key challenge for operational optical PNT (Positioning, Navigation, and Timing) systems. Optical satellite-to-ground links, such as those planned for ESA's OpSTAR mission, are vulnerable to atmospheric effects, particularly cloud cover, which can degrade or completely interrupt communications with an Optical Ground Station (OGS). The study will assess and experimentally demonstrate atmospheric transmission enhancement techniques designed to improve link availability under adverse weather conditions. It will evaluate whether these approaches can maintain accurate and reliable timing and ranging measurements between laser terminals representative of future operational optical PNT systems.
